<!-- Generated by docs-infra Python API -->

Independent pure-numpy parity oracle for `evoxc_hf`.

This module is the *reference implementation* the compiled `evoxc` graphs in
`evoxc_hf.models` are validated against.  It is deliberately written twice:
the graphs are built from `evoxc` ops, while everything here is plain numpy
written in a **different formulation** (explicit per-head Python loops,
hand-written mean/variance formulas, `math.erf`), so that a parity failure
points at exactly one of the two implementations and a shared bug would have to
be introduced twice, in two different shapes of code, to slip through.

Hard rules for this module:

* **numpy + stdlib only.**  Nothing here imports `evoxc`, `evoxc_hf.ops`,
  `evoxc_hf.config` or a family module — the one allowed `evoxc_hf` import is
  `evoxc_hf.errors.HFUnsupportedError` (for `resolve_activation`).
  Importing the graph code would make this oracle an echo of the thing it
  validates, which defeats its purpose.
* **float32 faithful.**  Every numeric input is normalised to
  `numpy.float32` and every numeric return value is `numpy.float32`,
  mirroring the fp32 HuggingFace modules these primitives reproduce.  `float64`
  inputs are therefore *downcast* (each docstring says so).  The only internal
  float64 pass is the `gelu_erf` `erf` evaluation, which is rounded back
  to float32 before returning.
* **Primitives, not models.**  This module holds the shared numeric pieces
  (softmax / norms / activations / RoPE / attention) plus `param_count`.
  The per-family forward passes live in the family modules and compose these
  helpers.
* **Explicit errors only.**  Malformed shapes, dtypes and static values raise
  `ValueError` / `TypeError` with a message naming the function, the
  argument and what was expected; unsupported activations raise
  `evoxc_hf.errors.HFUnsupportedError`.  No silent coercion, no fallback.

Layout conventions used throughout (HF's `LlamaForCausalLM` /
`GPT2LMHeadModel` layouts):

===============  ============================================================
`x`            `(..., d)` hidden states; `d` is the normalised/feature axis
`weight`       `(d,)` per-channel scale (HF `nn.LayerNorm` / RMSNorm shape)
`q/k/v`        `(batch, heads, seq, head_dim)` (attention, RoPE)
`cos/sin`      `(seq, head_dim)` RoPE tables
`mask`         `(seq, seq)` additive float mask (broadcastable)
===============  ============================================================

## Symbols

- [`additive_causal_mask`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/additive-causal-mask/) — Causal additive mask of shape `(seq_len, seq_len)` in float32.
- [`apply_rope`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/apply-rope/) — Rotate `x` with the HF `rotate_half` RoPE convention.
- [`attention`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/attention/) — Causal multi-head attention, one explicit Python loop per (batch, head).
- [`gelu_erf`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/gelu-erf/) — Exact (erf-form) GELU: `0.5 * x * (1 + erf(x / sqrt(2)))`.
- [`gelu_tanh`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/gelu-tanh/) — Tanh-approximated GELU — HF `gelu_new` / `gelu_pytorch_tanh`.
- [`layer_norm`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/layer-norm/) — HuggingFace `nn.LayerNorm` over the **last** axis (biased variance).
- [`param_count`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/param-count/) — Total number of scalar elements in a nested parameter tree.
- [`relu`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/relu/) — Rectified linear unit: `max(x, 0)`.
- [`resolve_activation`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/resolve-activation/) — Return the activation callable registered under `name`.
- [`rms_norm`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/rms-norm/) — HuggingFace `LlamaRMSNorm` over the **last** axis (no mean subtraction).
- [`rope_tables`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/rope-tables/) — Rotary-embedding cos/sin tables, bit-for-bit the HF computation.
- [`silu`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/silu/) — SiLU / swish: `x * sigmoid(x)`, evaluated in a numerically stable form.
- [`softmax`](/api/evoxc-hf/reference/softmax/) — Numerically stable softmax over `axis`.
